description:
Project: website — Restaurant de sushis

Business: Restaurant de sushis avec un menu à présenter.

Goal: Présenter le menu, permettre les commandes en ligne via une plateforme tierce, et faciliter le contact/réservation.

Target audience: Clients locaux souhaitant commander ou visiter.

Key features:
- Présentation du menu complet
- Bouton de commande vers plateforme tierce
- Carte avec emplacement
- Formulaire de contact
- Formulaire de réservation
- Galerie de photos

Design & brand:
- Colors: Rouge et blanc.
- Mood: Style japonais, dessins ou style anime.
- Signature: Plats mémorables mis en valeur par des photos (galerie).
- First impression: Unspecified.

designManifest.copyVoice: Quiet omakase host — short declarative present-tense French, sensory but never gushing, English following in a lighter register.
designManifest.heroThesis: The homepage opens on one perfect nigiri on warm washi white in 65% negative space — proof the kitchen treats sushi as calligraphy: precise, spare, unforgettable.
designManifest.iconDirection: A vermilion hanko-stamp rounded square on washi white, with a negative-space 'S' carved as a single confident brushstroke.
designManifest.signatureMove: Every section title pairs a horizontal French headline with its English translation set as a thin vertical ink rail (writing-mode: vertical-rl), and menu categories are chosen via vermilion hanko-stamp chips that press to a filled seal on click.
designManifest.summary: A washi-white gallery where each dish is treated like an ink-print exhibit — calm negative space, a single deep vermilion sealing the identity, and a bilingual vertical rail turning translation itself into ornament.
designManifest.typography: Shippori Mincho 600/700 for display headlines, the wordmark and prices (its Japanese-serif bones carry the culture); Karla 400/600 for body, menu and forms.

directions.pitch: Vos assiettes deviennent des estampes : un blanc washi calme, un rouge vermillon posé comme un sceau, et chaque photo de plat qui respire — c'est exactement l'expérience japonaise raffinée que vos clients viennent chercher, en salle comme à l'écran.

Pour les fringales de 21h : un site sombre et lumineux comme une izakaya de Tokyo, où le bouton Commander brille littéralement dans la nuit — pensé pour transformer l'envie du soir en commande en deux clics.

L'indigo sur porcelaine blanche vous distingue de tous les restos sushi rouge-et-blanc de la ville : chaque plat est présenté comme une pièce de collection, et le rouge — réservé aux prix et au bouton Commander — guide l'œil exactement là où votre chiffre d'affaires se joue.

promptHistory.changeNotes:
Build initial complet du PWA « Sushi Moodz » : identité Sumi & Vermillon (blanc washi, vermillon, encre) avec Shippori Mincho + Karla, rail bilingue vertical et filtres de menu en sceaux hanko. Pages : accueil, carte interactive, galerie, réservation, contact avec carte Google. Backend admin complet (menu, galerie, actualités, réservations, messages) via un shell générique, suivi des visites, formulaires réservation/contact reliés à la base et à l’email, bannières PWA/notifications, i18n FR/EN côté serveur.

Admin enrichment: (1) Dashboard now has a descriptive subtitle, clickable stat cards that link to their module, a 'Quick actions' panel, reservation status badges, richer 'recent messages' rows (email + longer excerpt), and clearer grouped/hinted settings form with per-field help. (2) Module CRUD pages (admin-shell + admin.js) upgraded: search retained, added a smart filter dropdown driven by the module's select field (e.g. reservation status, menu category), a live result counter, status/boolean rendered as colored badges, select values shown as human labels, better empty states, image thumbnails with placeholder, backdrop + Escape-to-close on the modal, disabled save button during submit, and prioritized inclusion of the status/category column so it's always visible. Full create/edit/delete remains intact for every module. (3) admin-styles.css: added focus-visible outlines, hover states, badge styles (ok/no/new), toolbar/filter/count styling, table row hover, modal shadow, button disabled state, --admin-brand alias, and improved responsive rules. (4) styles.css: added global focus-visible outlines for accessibility. All existing routes, data flow, i18n keys, editable-content annotations and {{IMG_*}} placeholder tokens preserved byte-for-byte. No functional collections were hardcoded — menu items (with price, category, availability, featured, sort order) and other operational data were already fully admin-managed.

Removed the duplicated full-carte section from the homepage (rank 1) and replaced it with a single outlined 'La carte' link inside the Signatures section; fixed the sticky menu filter's top offset to clear the sticky header on mobile and added a hover:none rule so gallery captions render on touch devices (rank 2/4, same file); added a native min date to the reservation form to block past dates (rank 3); wired active-page highlighting into the admin sidebar via a typeof-guarded moduleKey (rank 5); added inline color fallback + aria-pressed toggling to the menu category chips in both the EJS partial and app.js click handler (rank 6/7); localized the carte/galerie/reserver page titles by req.lang while leaving contact as-is (rank 8); and added inline white/vermilion fallback styles to the order-band CTAs on both index.ejs and carte.ejs (rank 9/10). All image placeholders, data-* annotations, and platform wiring were preserved untouched.
